relevance_note: Case series of three children with HA20 in which the authors state "Genetic testing showed that all three patients had heterozygous mutation in TNFAIP3 gene." and describe each child's clinical features, variant and treatment, plus the mother and father of Patient 3.
method_note: Read the whole Markdown file (including figure legends and the reference list) together with the schema and the rules; no script was used, every row was transcribed by hand from the paper text. Decisions and contradictions found in the paper: (1) Table 1 and Table 2 carry no legend defining '+' or '-' (or 'N'), so per the rules those symbols were not used as evidence of presence or absence; all features come from the narrative text. (2) The sentence 'The sites of gene mutation in TNFAIP3 in those 3 patients were c.1906 + 1G > C heterozygous mutation, c.925_927dup heterozygous mutation, and c.547C > T heterozygous mutation.' lists the variants in an order that contradicts the per-patient sections (Patient 1 = c.925-927dup, Patient 2 = c.1906 + 1G > C, Patient 3 = c.547C > T); I followed the per-patient sections. (3) Figure citations are inconsistent: Patient 2's text cites Fig. 4 for her mutation map and Patient 3's text cites Fig. 5, while the markdown figure legends for Fig. 3/4/5 are shifted (the CT/MRI legend appears under Fig. 5). (4) Patient 1 is introduced as a girl but the physical-examination sentence calls the patient 'a 91 cm and 11.5 kg boy'. (5) Table 1 shows renal damage '+' for Patient 2 while the text reports normal urine tests and 24-h proteinuria; because the symbol is undefined and the two statements conflict, renal damage was recorded for nobody. (6) 'c.1906 + 1G > C and c.925_927dup were confirmed by Sanger sequencing as spontaneous mutations.' was read as de novo for Patients 1 and 2 (recorded in inheritance); the paper does not print the individual parental results. (7) No per-variant class or pathogenicity statement is printed ('our 3 patients showed the possibility of pathogenicity at genetic level' is hedged and cohort-level), so variant_type_as_stated and pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors are 'not reported'; the only functional comments (OTU domain location, possible effect on splicing) are predictions, not assay results. (8) The Discussion's literature survey (24 articles, 35 patients in 14 families) is given only as counts or as unnamed 'one case' statements, so no rows were created for those people. (9) The parents of Patients 1 and 2 are named only in the figure legends ('Map of gene mutations of Patient 1's father'); Methods state blood was collected from each child and their parents, so they are included as relatives, but no variant description is printed for them and no variant row was created. (10) The paper prints only ages at admission; these are recorded in age_at_last_evaluation, and age at onset and age at diagnosis are 'not reported'. (11) Absence of a narrow item was not used for composite checklist items: 'no rash' and 'no eye discomfort' leave the checklist items 'skin lesions (rash, folliculitis, erythema nodosum)' and 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' as 'not reported', and Patient 3's 'no joint swelling and pain' was read as excluding 'arthritis or arthralgia' because the paper uses the pair as one phrase for this patient. (12) Normal whole-investigation findings (thoracic/abdominal CT, cellular immunity, urine tests, neutrophil phagocytosis) were not turned into feature rows. (13) No table cell contains ' / ' stacked values, so the stacked-cell rule did not apply. (14) is_proband is false for everyone (nobody is called a proband or index case, and no single-patient case report); no quote can support a false value, so those spans are null. (15) In the phenotype_checklist table the individual_label_in_paper cell has span null in every row: the label and its supporting quote are given once, in the individuals table, and repeating the same quote 20 times per person adds nothing. checklist_feature spans are null by rule. The evidence_basis cell also has span null everywhere: where the status is 'not reported' that is the missing value, and where the status is 'observed' or 'excluded' the quote is already in the status cell of the same row (and in the matching phenotypic_features row). (16) n_patients_reported is 3 because the authors state '3 children with HA20' as their patients; the mother of Patient 3 also carries a TNFAIP3 variant but is described as a relative, not as one of the study's patients. (17) The two rows for the mother of Patient 3 are deliberate: the paper states her oral and genital ulcers in two separate sentences (the Case 3 section and the Discussion), and I kept one feature row per statement rather than merging them; her checklist rows are the union of the two.
